intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

selected_hotel.name: Sultanahmet district, Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a morning exploring the iconic Hagia Sophia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum over its 1,500-year history. Walk across Sultanahmet Square to the stunning Blue Mosque, admiring its six minarets and intricate Iznik tile interior. Hire a local guide for deeper historical context on Byzantine and Ottoman architecture.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Bazaar Food and Shopping Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the Grand Bazaar, one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Then head to the nearby Egyptian Spice Bazaar to sample Turkish delight, saffron, dried fruits, and local spices. Chat with vendors, taste free samples, and pick up authentic local products. A guided food walk here adds rich storytelling about Ottoman trade history.

experiences.name: Bosphorus Strait Sunset Cruise
experiences.description: Board a traditional wooden boat for a scenic cruise along the Bosphorus Strait, the waterway dividing Europe and Asia. Marvel at Ottoman-era palaces like Dolmabahçe and Beylerbeyi, historic yalı waterfront mansions, and the iconic Bosphorus Bridge at golden hour. Many local ferries offer affordable public routes that double as sightseeing experiences.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Harem Tour
experiences.description: Explore Topkapi Palace, the administrative heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Walk through the Imperial Treasury to see priceless jewels and artifacts, visit the sacred relics pavilion, and take a guided tour of the Harem — the private royal quarters with elaborately decorated rooms. The palace gardens offer breathtaking panoramic views over the Golden Horn and Bosphorus.

experiences.name: Traditional Turkish Cooking Class & Meyhane Dinner
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in the bohemian Karaköy neighborhood where a local chef teaches you to prepare classic dishes like meze, börek, and lamb kebabs using fresh market ingredients. In the evening, dine at a traditional meyhane (Turkish tavern) in Beyoğlu, enjoying rakı, fresh seafood, and live fasıl music — a true immersion into Istanbul's vibrant food and social culture.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Sultanahmet district, Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use this time to rest on the plane.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly Havaist airport bus (approx. 100-120 TRY) to Sultanahmet. Check into Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay, freshen up, then take a gentle orientation walk around Sultanahmet Square. Admire the exterior of the Blue Mosque and the Hagia Sophia from outside — both are free to view externally. Get your bearings for the days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Hippodrome (At Meydanı), a free open-air historical site with the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column. Explore the surrounding streets of Sultanahmet as the city lights up at dusk.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap simit (sesame bread ring) and ayran from a street cart near Sultanahmet Square for around 30-40 TRY.
meals.dinner: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi — a legendary, budget-friendly köfte (meatball) restaurant steps from the Hippodrome. A full meal with köfte, bread, and ayran costs around 150-200 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some cash at a reputable currency exchange office (döviz bürosu) in Sultanahmet — avoid airport exchange rates. Pick up an Istanbul Kart (transport card) at the metro station for cheap tram and ferry rides throughout your trip.

day_by_day.morning: Start early at the Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) — one of the world's greatest architectural marvels. Entry is free as it is now an active mosque; dress modestly and bring a scarf. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring its Byzantine mosaics, massive dome, and layered history spanning nearly 1,500 years.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk five minutes to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) — also free entry. Marvel at its six minarets and stunning Iznik tile interior. Afterwards, visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı), an underground Byzantine water reservoir with atmospheric lighting and ancient Medusa column bases (entry approx. 200 TRY).
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the Grand Bazaar neighborhood for a pre-dinner wander through the atmospheric backstreets of Çemberlitaş. Visit the Çemberlitaş Hamamı area and soak in the old-city atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your hotel or grab a classic Turkish breakfast (tea, cheese, olives, egg) at a local kahvaltı spot near the hotel for 80-120 TRY.
meals.lunch: Eat at Hafız Mustafa 1864 near the Basilica Cistern — try a börek (flaky pastry) and a Turkish tea for around 100-150 TRY.
meals.dinner: Head to Çiçek Pasajı-style side streets near Divan Yolu for a pide (Turkish flatbread pizza) at a local fırın (bakery-restaurant) for 100-160 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Mosque closes to tourists during prayer times (5 times daily, ~90 minutes each). Check the schedule in advance and plan your visit between prayers. Modest dress is mandatory for both mosques.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapı Palace, the opulent heart of the Ottoman Empire for over 400 years. Budget around 3 hours to explore the courtyards, the Imperial Treasury, and the Harem (separate ticket). Entry approx. 700-900 TRY total. Book tickets online to avoid queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the adjacent Gülhane Park — a beautiful and free public park that was once the outer garden of Topkapı. Stroll down to the waterfront and enjoy views of the Bosphorus and the Sea of Marmara. Visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums complex nearby (entry approx. 200 TRY) — world-class ancient artifacts including the Alexander Sarcophagus.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet and explore the lively Arasta Bazaar, a quieter and less touristy alternative to the Grand Bazaar, right behind the Blue Mosque. Browse handmade ceramics, textiles, and spices without high-pressure sales tactics.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast at the hotel or a local café near Sultanahmet for 80-120 TRY.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic from a nearby bakkal (corner store) — bread, cheese, tomatoes, olives — and eat in Gülhane Park for under 80 TRY.
meals.dinner: Try Develi Restaurant's budget-friendly sister eatery or a local kebap house on Divan Yolu for an Adana or Urfa kebap meal for 180-230 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: The Topkapı Harem requires a separate ticket and guided entry — buy it at the Harem entrance inside the palace. Monday is a good day to visit as crowds are lighter than weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Cross the Golden Horn by tram (T1 line) to the Eminönü waterfront. Explore the iconic Egyptian Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) — free entry — and sample Turkish delight, dried fruits, spices, and teas. Haggle politely for the best prices on souvenirs and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up the hill to the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — the world's oldest and largest covered market with over 4,000 shops. Entry is free. Get intentionally lost in its labyrinthine streets, discover artisan workshops, and enjoy the sensory overload of color, sound, and scent.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the Süleymaniye Mosque — arguably the most architecturally perfect Ottoman mosque, designed by the legendary architect Mimar Sinan. Free entry. Enjoy panoramic views over the Golden Horn from its terrace garden at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh simit and tea from a street vendor at Eminönü waterfront — a true Istanbul morning ritual for under 40 TRY.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Spice Bazaar food stalls or nearby Hamdi Restaurant's budget annex for a lamb döner wrap and ayran for 120-160 TRY.
meals.dinner: Dine at one of the humble lokanta (traditional Turkish canteen) restaurants near Süleymaniye — hearty home-cooked stews, rice, and salad for 120-180 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Tuesday is ideal for a visit. Beware of carpet shop invitations — politely decline if you're not interested. Keep your belongings secure in crowded bazaars.

day_by_day.morning: Take the T1 tram to Karaköy, then the Tünel funicular (one of the world's oldest underground railways, built in 1875) up to Beyoğlu. Walk along the famous İstiklal Avenue — a 1.4 km pedestrian boulevard lined with 19th-century European-style architecture, bookshops, music stores, and cafés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the side streets of Beyoğlu: visit Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage), the historic fish market of Balık Pazarı, and the Armenian, Greek, and Catholic churches tucked between the buildings. Walk to Galata Tower (entry approx. 200 TRY) for sweeping 360° views of Istanbul, the Bosphorus, and the Golden Horn.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Beyoğlu for the evening. Explore the hip Karaköy neighborhood on the way back — full of street art, independent coffee shops, and a thriving arts scene. Take the tram back to Sultanahmet.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a traditional Turkish breakfast house (kahvaltı salonu) in Karaköy — full spread of cheeses, eggs, honey, and tea for 150-200 TRY.
meals.lunch: Grab a midye dolma (stuffed mussels) from a street cart on İstiklal Avenue — a beloved Istanbul street food, typically 10-15 TRY per piece.
meals.dinner: Eat at a meyhane (Turkish tavern) in the Nevizade Street area off İstiklal — mezze plates, fish, and raki for a full experience around 300-400 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: İstiklal Avenue is very crowded on evenings and weekends. The nostalgic red tram runs along İstiklal — a fun, cheap ride. Galata Tower can have long queues; consider going just before closing for smaller crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Bosphorus ferry from Eminönü to Üsküdar on the Asian side (approx. 20-30 TRY with Istanbul Kart) — one of the world's great short ferry crossings. Explore Üsküdar's authentic neighborhood feel, visit the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque, and enjoy the Bosphorus waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Kadıköy — Istanbul's vibrant, bohemian Asian-side neighborhood. Explore the Kadıköy Market (Kadıköy Çarşısı), packed with fresh produce, cheese shops, fish stalls, and street food. Browse the indie bookshops and record stores on Moda Caddesi.
day_by_day.evening: Take the ferry back from Kadıköy to Eminönü at sunset — one of the most beautiful views in Istanbul as the city's silhouette glows golden. Walk back to your hotel through Sultanahmet.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel or grab tea and pastry at a local bakery in Sultanahmet before the ferry.
meals.lunch: Eat in Kadıköy Market — try kokoreç (seasoned offal sandwich), fresh fish sandwich, or a plate of meze from market stalls for 80-150 TRY.
meals.dinner: Back in Sultanahmet, try Buhara 93 Restaurant for traditional Turkish home cooking — lentil soup, grilled chicken, and pilaf for 180-220 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: Kadıköy is considered more 'local' and less touristy than the European side — prices are lower and the atmosphere is relaxed. Keep your Istanbul Kart topped up for ferry rides.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — a Byzantine masterpiece covered in some of the finest surviving medieval mosaics and frescoes in the world. Take the T1 tram to Aksaray then a short taxi (approx. 80-100 TRY). Entry approx. 200 TRY.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the ancient Theodosian Walls — the 5th-century land walls that protected Constantinople for over 1,000 years. Explore the Edirnekapı gate area and walk a section of the walls for free. Take a taxi or bus back toward Fatih neighborhood to visit the Fatih Mosque complex.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet via tram. Enjoy a peaceful evening at the Hippodrome, now beautifully lit at night. Visit a traditional Turkish tea house (çay bahçesi) in the area and play backgammon with locals.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local esnaf lokantası (tradesmen's canteen) near Fatih Mosque — daily specials like lamb stew, bulgur pilaf, and soup for 100-150 TRY.
meals.dinner: Try Şehzade Erzurum Cağ Kebabı near Sultanahmet — famous for cağ kebabı (horizontal spit-roasted lamb) for 200-250 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: Friday is the Islamic holy day — the Fatih Mosque will be very busy for Friday noon prayers (around 13:00). Plan your visit before or after. The Chora Church may have limited hours; check ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Take the T1 tram to Kabataş, then the funicular to Taksim Square. From Taksim, take a taxi or bus to the Dolmabahçe Palace on the Bosphorus shore — the lavish 19th-century Ottoman palace that replaced Topkapı. Guided tours only (approx. 500-700 TRY). Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk south along the Bosphorus waterfront through Beşiktaş neighborhood — a lively, local district. Explore the Beşiktaş fish market and the waterfront tea gardens. Take the ferry or bus back toward Eminönü.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Rüstem Pasha Mosque near Eminönü — a hidden gem designed by Mimar Sinan, tucked above a row of shops. Free entry. Its interior is completely covered in stunning Iznik tiles. Enjoy the Golden Horn waterfront at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast near Taksim — a classic Turkish breakfast sandwich (tost) from a street kiosk for 60-80 TRY.
meals.lunch: Eat in Beşiktaş at a local balık ekmek (fish sandwich) stall by the ferry pier — fresh grilled fish in bread for 80-100 TRY.
meals.dinner: Dine at Pandeli Restaurant near the Spice Bazaar (historic but moderately priced) or a nearby lokanta for soup, stew, and bread for 150-200 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires separate tickets for different sections. The Ceremonial Hall is the highlight — prioritize that if budget is tight. Saturday can be crowded; arrive early.

day_by_day.morning: Take the T1 tram to Eminönü and board the public ferry (Şehir Hatları) for the classic Bosphorus cruise from Eminönü to Anadolu Kavağı — a 90-minute scenic journey past Ottoman palaces, wooden yalı mansions, and medieval fortresses for only 60-80 TRY each way. Departs at 10:35 on weekdays and weekends.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Anadolu Kavağı, a charming fishing village at the mouth of the Black Sea. Hike up to the ruined Yoros Castle (Genoese Castle) for panoramic views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. Explore the village and its fish restaurants.
day_by_day.evening: Take the return ferry back to Eminönü (departs around 15:00-16:00). Arrive back in Sultanahmet by early evening. Relax and reflect on the incredible Bosphorus scenery.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel before departing early for the ferry.
meals.lunch: Eat fresh grilled fish at one of the waterfront fish restaurants in Anadolu Kavağı — grilled sea bass or bream with salad and bread for 200-280 TRY.
meals.dinner: Light dinner back in Sultanahmet — mercimek çorbası (lentil soup) and gözleme (stuffed flatbread) from a street food stall for 100-140 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: The Bosphorus public ferry is one of Istanbul's greatest budget experiences — far cheaper than private tour boats. Buy your Istanbul Kart tokens before boarding. Check the current ferry timetable at Şehir Hatları website as schedules can vary seasonally.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the historic Zeyrek neighborhood — a UNESCO-listed area of wooden Ottoman houses on the hill above the Golden Horn. Visit the Zeyrek Mosque (formerly the Pantokrator Monastery Church), a stunning Byzantine church complex from the 12th century. Free entry. Wander the atmospheric cobblestone streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Balat and Fener neighborhoods — two of Istanbul's oldest and most atmospheric districts, home to ancient Greek Orthodox, Jewish, and Armenian communities. Explore the colorful painted houses of Balat, visit the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople in Fener (free entry), and browse the antique shops and vintage stores.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Golden Horn waterfront promenade back toward Eminönü and take the tram home to Sultanahmet. Enjoy a relaxed evening at a rooftop tea garden with Bosphorus views.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Eat at a tiny meyhane or lokanta in Balat — the neighborhood has several charming, cheap local restaurants. Full meal for 120-160 TRY.
meals.dinner: Try Balıkçı Sabahattin near Sultanahmet — a classic Istanbul fish restaurant. Order the daily catch with salad and bread for 250-320 TRY (a slight splurge but worth it).

day_by_day.notes: Balat and Fener are best explored on foot. The streets are hilly and uneven — wear comfortable shoes. This area is increasingly popular with photographers and artists, so it's lively but not yet overcrowded with tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts (Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi) on the Hippodrome — a world-class collection of carpets, calligraphy, ceramics, and manuscripts in a stunning 16th-century palace. Entry approx. 200 TRY. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the tram to Beyazıt and explore the Istanbul University area and the historic Beyazıt Mosque (free entry). Walk through the Sahaflar Çarşısı (Old Book Bazaar) — a charming outdoor book market selling antique and secondhand books, maps, and manuscripts. Then revisit the Grand Bazaar for any last-minute shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Walk up to the Süleymaniye neighborhood for a final sunset view over the Golden Horn from the mosque terrace. Explore the traditional Ottoman hans (caravanserais) and workshops in the area.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the student-friendly lokanta restaurants near Istanbul University — filling meals for 100-140 TRY.
meals.dinner: Try Khorasani Restaurant near the Grand Bazaar for southeastern Turkish cuisine — kebaps, lahmacun, and mezze for 200-260 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: The Sahaflar Book Bazaar is a wonderful place to find antique Ottoman maps and prints as unique, affordable souvenirs. Prices are negotiable. The area around Beyazıt is lively with university students — a great insight into modern Istanbul life.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Princes' Islands (Adalar) — a group of car-free islands in the Sea of Marmara, just 1-2 hours by ferry from Kabataş pier. Take the ferry to Büyükada, the largest island (approx. 50-70 TRY with Istanbul Kart). Rent a bicycle (100-150 TRY/day) and explore the island's Victorian mansions, pine forests, and quiet beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue cycling or walking around Büyükada. Visit the hilltop Aya Yorgi Monastery for panoramic sea views. Relax on the rocky shoreline and swim if weather permits. Enjoy the tranquil, traffic-free atmosphere — a stark contrast to the city.
day_by_day.evening: Take the ferry back to Kabataş as the sun sets over the Sea of Marmara — a magical experience. Return to Sultanahmet by tram.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel before the early ferry departure.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the island's fish restaurants near the ferry pier — grilled fish plate for 200-250 TRY, or grab a cheaper sandwich from a bakery.
meals.dinner: Final special dinner in Sultanahmet — try Mozaik Restaurant for a sit-down Ottoman-Turkish dinner with Bosphorus views. Budget 300-400 TRY for a full meal with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Check the Şehir Hatları ferry timetable for Büyükada departures from Kabataş — ferries run multiple times daily. The island gets crowded on weekends; Wednesday is ideal. Horse-drawn carriages (fayton) are available but more expensive than bicycles.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul. Revisit your favorite spot one last time — whether it's the Hagia Sophia at sunrise, the Bosphorus waterfront, or a quiet tea house. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at the Arasta Bazaar (best prices in Sultanahmet). Pack your bags.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and head to the airport. Take the Havaist airport bus from Sultanahmet/Aksaray (approx. 100-120 TRY) — allow 60-90 minutes travel time plus airport check-in time. Depart Istanbul.
day_by_day.evening: En route home. Reflect on 13 incredible days of Byzantine mosaics, Ottoman grandeur, Bosphorus sunsets, and unforgettable Turkish food.

meals.breakfast: Final full Turkish breakfast — treat yourself to a proper spread at a Sultanahmet breakfast café for 150-200 TRY. Enjoy çay, fresh bread, honey, kaymak (clotted cream), and eggs one last time.
meals.lunch: Quick and easy — grab a döner wrap or lahmacun (Turkish flatbread with minced meat) from a street stall near the hotel for 80-100 TRY before heading to the airport.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Leave at least 3 hours before your flight for the journey to Istanbul Airport. The Havaist bus is the cheapest option; a taxi will cost 600-900 TRY. Make sure to use up remaining Turkish Lira on snacks, tea, and last souvenirs — currency is hard to exchange back abroad. Return your Istanbul Kart at a machine to get your deposit back (approx. 50 TRY).

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Sultanahmet district, Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from Istanbul Airport to Sultanahmet hotel via airport bus (Havaist) or metro+tram. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Easy orientation walk around Sultanahmet Square. Stroll past the exterior of the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia to get your bearings. Visit the Hippodrome (At Meydanı) and see the Obelisk of Theodosius, the Serpent Column, and the German Fountain — all free and just steps from the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric streets of Sultanahmet at dusk. Enjoy your first Bosphorus view from the waterfront promenade near Eminönü. Settle into the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a simit (sesame bread ring) and tea from a street cart near the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light snack at the hotel or a quick pide (Turkish flatbread) at a lokanta near Sultanahmet Square — budget ~150–200 TL.
meals.dinner: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi (Historic Sultanahmet Meatball Restaurant) on Divanyolu Caddesi — a legendary, affordable local institution serving köfte with white beans and bread. Budget ~200–300 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 relaxed — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Focus on arriving safely, settling in, and getting a feel for the neighborhood. Exchange some cash at a reputable exchange office (döviz bürosu) in Sultanahmet for better rates than airport kiosks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya Camii) first thing when it opens to beat the crowds. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring this architectural marvel that has served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum over 1,500 years. Note: dress modestly and bring a scarf for women.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) — free entry, stunning interior with 20,000 Iznik tiles. Then explore Topkapi Palace, the seat of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years. Visit the Harem (separate ticket), Treasury, and Imperial Kitchens. Budget 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Take a short walk down to the Arasta Bazaar (behind the Blue Mosque) for souvenir browsing. Enjoy sunset views from the terrace of a rooftop café overlooking the Sea of Marmara.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast (kahvaltı) at the hotel or at Café Mesale near the Arasta Bazaar — olives, cheese, eggs, honey, tomatoes, tea. Budget ~150–200 TL.
meals.lunch: Develi Restaurant or Balıkçı Sabahattin near the waterfront — try lahmacun (Turkish pizza) or mercimek çorbası (lentil soup) with fresh bread. Budget ~200–300 TL.
meals.dinner: Matbah Restaurant in the Ottoman Hotel Imperial — refined Ottoman cuisine in a historic setting without being overly expensive. Try Ottoman lamb stew or stuffed quince. Budget ~400–600 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is closed on Tuesdays — Sunday is perfect. Book Topkapi tickets online in advance to skip queues. Wear comfortable shoes — the palace grounds are vast. Prayer times at Hagia Sophia and Blue Mosque mean brief closures to tourists; check the schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with 4,000+ shops. Arrive early (opens 9:00) to enjoy it before crowds peak. Browse carpets, ceramics, jewelry, spices, and textiles. Practice your bargaining skills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes downhill to the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü. Browse exotic spices, Turkish delight, dried fruits, and teas. Then explore the surrounding Eminönü waterfront — watch ferries, fishermen on Galata Bridge, and the busy harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Galata Bridge on foot (great views) and climb to the Galata Tower neighborhood. Explore the bohemian streets of Karaköy and have dinner in this trendy district.

meals.breakfast: Simit Sarayı or a traditional tea house inside the Grand Bazaar area — simit, börek, and çay. Budget ~100–150 TL.
meals.lunch: Balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from the iconic floating boats at Eminönü waterfront — a quintessential Istanbul street food experience. Add a cup of fresh pomegranate juice. Budget ~80–120 TL.
meals.dinner: Karaköy Lokantası in Karaköy — beloved neighborhood restaurant with daily changing mezes and mains. Try cold mezes followed by grilled fish or slow-cooked lamb. Budget ~350–500 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays, so Monday is ideal. Carry small bills for street food and bazaar purchases. Beware of carpet shop owners who invite you for 'free tea' — it often leads to high-pressure sales. Enjoy the tea, but feel free to say no.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums complex (Arkeoloji Müzeleri) — three museums in one, including the main Archaeology Museum with the stunning Alexander Sarcophagus, the Museum of the Ancient Orient, and the Tiled Kiosk. One of Turkey's finest museum complexes, often overlooked by tourists.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Gülhane Park adjacent to the museum — a lovely Ottoman garden great for a picnic or a stroll. Then walk along the historic walls toward Cağaloğlu and visit the Cağaloğlu Hamam (one of Istanbul's oldest Turkish baths, built 1741) for a traditional hammam experience — scrub, foam massage, and relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Divanyolu Caddesi (the ancient Byzantine Mese road) back toward Sultanahmet. Browse independent bookshops and antique stores in the Sahaflar Çarşısı (Old Book Bazaar) area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Şükrü Usta near Sultanahmet — menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) and tea. Budget ~150–200 TL.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Gülhane Park — grab fresh bread, cheese, olives, and fruit from a nearby market (bakkal). Budget ~100–150 TL.
meals.dinner: Hamdi Restaurant near Eminönü — multiple floors with Bosphorus views, excellent kebabs and mezes. Try the beyti kebab or adana kebab. Budget ~350–500 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Cağaloğlu Hamam charges around 700–1,000 TL for the full tourist package (scrub + foam massage + towels). Book ahead or arrive early. Note that Topkapi Palace is closed today (Tuesday) — no conflict since we visited on Day 2. The Archaeological Museums are closed on Mondays, so Tuesday is perfect.

day_by_day.morning: Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day — a national holiday with parades and festivities. Head to Taksim Square in the morning to witness the official ceremonies and flag displays. Take the nostalgic tram (T2) along İstiklal Caddesi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore İstiklal Caddesi (Independence Avenue) — Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard with 19th-century European architecture, embassies, churches, and 3 km of shops and cafés. Branch off into side streets like Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage) and Balık Pazarı (Fish Market).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Beyoğlu neighborhood's vibrant nightlife streets — Nevizade Sokak and surrounding meyhanes (traditional taverns) for a lively evening of rakı, mezes, and live music.

meals.breakfast: Mandabatmaz in Beyoğlu — famous for its thick, traditional Turkish coffee. Pair with a pastry from a nearby bakery. Budget ~100–150 TL.
meals.lunch: Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage) — grab a table at one of the historic meyhanes for a midday meze spread. Try arnavut ciğeri (Albanian-style liver), haydari (yogurt dip), and stuffed mussels (midye dolma). Budget ~250–400 TL.
meals.dinner: Nevizade Sokak meyhane dinner — pick any of the lively restaurants with outdoor tables. Order rakı (anise spirit) with a selection of cold and hot mezes, followed by grilled fish. Budget ~400–600 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: May 19 is a national holiday — some museums may have adjusted hours or free entry. Taksim will be very busy in the morning with ceremonies. The nostalgic tram on İstiklal runs frequently and is a fun, authentic experience. Rakı is traditionally drunk with water and ice — ask the waiter to show you the proper way.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Bosphorus ferry cruise — board a public ferry (İDO/Şehir Hatları) from Eminönü or Beşiktaş for the classic long Bosphorus tour (approx. 1.5–2 hours each way) passing under the Bosphorus Bridge, past wooden yalıs (waterfront mansions), and up toward the Black Sea entrance at Anadolu Kavağı.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Anadolu Kavağı — a charming fishing village on the Asian side. Hike up to the ruined Yoros Castle (Genoese Castle) for panoramic views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. Explore the village.
day_by_day.evening: Take the return ferry back to Eminönü as the sun sets over the European skyline — one of Istanbul's most magical views. Return to Sultanahmet for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick börek from a pastane (pastry shop) near the ferry terminal. Budget ~100–150 TL.
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish lunch at one of the waterfront restaurants in Anadolu Kavağı — try levrek (sea bass) or çipura (sea bream) with salad and bread. Budget ~300–450 TL per person.
meals.dinner: Balıkçı Sabahattin in Sultanahmet — a beloved fish restaurant in a historic building with a garden. Try the meze spread followed by the catch of the day. Budget ~400–600 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry is extremely affordable (around 50–80 TL each way) and far better value than private tour boats. Buy an Istanbulkart (transit card) if you haven't already — it works on ferries, trams, and buses. The full Bosphorus tour runs a few times daily; check the Şehir Hatları schedule in advance. Bring a light jacket as it can be breezy on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul via ferry from Eminönü to Kadıköy — a vibrant, local neighborhood largely untouched by mass tourism. Explore the Kadıköy Produce Market (Tarihi Kadıköy Çarşısı) — a sensory feast of fresh produce, spices, cheeses, olives, and street food.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll along Moda Caddesi — Kadıköy's charming seaside promenade popular with locals. Visit Moda Park for city views. Browse the independent bookshops, vintage stores, and street art in the Yeldeğirmeni neighborhood. Take the ferry back to Eminönü in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — Sinan's masterpiece built for Suleiman the Magnificent (1557). Less crowded than the Blue Mosque, equally magnificent, and set on a hilltop with sweeping city views. The mosque complex includes a historic cemetery and medrese buildings.

meals.breakfast: Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy — one of Istanbul's most celebrated restaurants for authentic Anatolian cuisine. Their breakfast spread features regional dishes from across Turkey. Budget ~200–300 TL.
meals.lunch: Graze through Kadıköy Market — try kokoreç (seasoned offal sandwich), tantuni (spiced meat wrap), fresh fish sandwiches, and ayran (yogurt drink). Budget ~150–200 TL for a market lunch.
meals.dinner: Tarihi Karadeniz Pide ve Kebap Salonu near Sultanahmet — a no-frills, authentic lokanta serving pide (Turkish flatbread pizza) and kebabs loved by locals. Try the kuşbaşılı pide (pide with diced meat). Budget ~200–300 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: Friday is Cuma (Friday prayer) — the Süleymaniye Mosque will be closed to tourists during midday prayer (approximately 12:30–14:00). Plan your visit for late afternoon/early evening. Kadıköy is very much a local neighborhood — a great contrast to the touristy Historic Peninsula. The ferry ride itself (about 20 minutes) is a highlight.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii/Museum) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — home to some of the finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, rivaling those of Ravenna. Take tram T1 toward Eminönü and then a taxi or bus to Edirnekapı.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the ancient Theodosian Land Walls — the 5th-century Byzantine fortifications that protected Constantinople for 1,000 years. The walls stretch for kilometers and offer a fascinating, atmospheric walk through history. Visit the Yedikule Fortress (Seven Towers Castle) at the southern end.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel and refresh, then head to the Balat and Fener neighborhoods — Istanbul's historic Jewish and Greek Orthodox quarters along the Golden Horn. Wander colorful Ottoman-era streets and visit the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a traditional Turkish breakfast at a local tea garden near Sultanahmet.
meals.lunch: Asitane Restaurant near the Chora Church — serving recreated Ottoman palace recipes based on historical records. Unique and memorable. Budget ~400–600 TL per person.
meals.dinner: Fener/Balat neighborhood — try Agora Meyhanesi (a historic Greek-style meyhane) or one of the charming small restaurants in Balat's colorful streets. Budget ~300–450 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Chora Church/Kariye has had varying opening status — verify current access before visiting as restoration work has affected access in recent years. The Theodosian Walls are best explored with a map or guide app as the area is spread out. Wear sturdy walking shoes for the walls. Balat and Fener are best explored on foot — the streets are hilly and atmospheric.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Dolmabahçe Palace in Beşiktaş — the lavish 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus shore where Atatürk spent his final days. The opulent European-Ottoman fusion architecture is extraordinary. Guided tours are mandatory and run regularly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Beşiktaş waterfront and explore the lively Beşiktaş neighborhood — a bustling, authentic district popular with university students and locals. Visit the Beşiktaş open-air market (on Sundays) for local produce and goods.
day_by_day.evening: Take a taxi or bus to Ortaköy — a picturesque Bosphorus village beneath the Bosphorus Bridge. Browse the Sunday artisan market, admire the ornate Ortaköy Mosque reflected in the water, and enjoy the vibrant café and restaurant scene.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Güllüoğlu in Karaköy — Istanbul's most famous baklava and börek shop. Try the su böreği (water pastry) and a glass of tea. Budget ~150–200 TL.
meals.lunch: Beşiktaş market area — try a lahmacun roll, fresh simit, or one of the market food stalls. Budget ~100–150 TL.
meals.dinner: Ortaköy waterfront restaurants — try kumpir (massive stuffed baked potato, a local specialty) as a snack, then sit down for dinner at one of the Bosphorus-view restaurants. Try grilled sea bass or shrimp güveç (clay pot). Budget ~400–600 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays — Sunday is ideal. Book tickets online in advance as tour groups fill up quickly. Photography inside the palace is restricted. Ortaköy is extremely popular on Sunday evenings — arrive for dinner before 19:00 to avoid long waits. The kumpir stalls in Ortaköy are a beloved Istanbul street food tradition.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts (Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi) on the Hippodrome — housed in the Ibrahim Pasha Palace, it contains extraordinary collections of carpets, calligraphy, manuscripts, and ethnographic exhibits showing Ottoman and Islamic life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — the magnificent 6th-century underground Byzantine water cistern with 336 marble columns, atmospheric lighting, and the famous Medusa head bases. Then walk to the Little Hagia Sophia (Küçük Ayasofya Camii) — a stunning 6th-century Byzantine church converted to a mosque, often overlooked.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Sea of Marmara waterfront (Kennedy Caddesi) from Sultanahmet toward Kumkapı — Istanbul's historic fishing and seafood district. Enjoy the sea breeze and harbor views.

meals.breakfast: Sefa Restaurant near Sultanahmet — a beloved, no-frills lokanta (workers' restaurant) serving homestyle Turkish food. Try menemen or lentil soup with bread. Budget ~120–180 TL.
meals.lunch: Sultanahmet Köftecisi or similar lokanta near the Basilica Cistern. Budget ~200–300 TL.
meals.dinner: Kumkapı neighborhood — a labyrinth of seafood restaurants with live music and street vendors. Try a mixed fish platter (karışık balık tabağı) with mezes and rakı. Budget ~400–600 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Basilica Cistern underwent major renovation — verify current opening status and book tickets online as capacity may be limited. Little Hagia Sophia is free and rarely crowded — a hidden gem. Kumkapı can be touristy but remains a fun, lively experience — bargain a bit on the restaurant menu prices if approached by a host on the street.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a ferry from Kabataş or Eminönü to Büyükada (the largest island, about 1.5 hours). No motor vehicles are allowed — explore by horse-drawn carriage (fayton) or bicycle. Visit the hilltop Aya Yorgi Monastery with panoramic sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Büyükada — rent a bicycle and cycle around the island's pine-scented paths past Victorian-era wooden mansions. Swim at one of the small beaches if weather permits (May can be warm enough). Catch the late afternoon ferry back to Istanbul.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by ferry, arriving at Kabataş or Eminönü by early evening. Relaxed dinner in Sultanahmet or Karaköy.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before the ferry — simit and tea at the Kabataş/Eminönü ferry terminal. Budget ~80–120 TL.
meals.lunch: Büyükada waterfront restaurants — fresh fish and mezes with island views. Try the grilled squid or sea bream. Budget ~300–450 TL per person.
meals.dinner: Zübeyir Ocakbaşı in Beyoğlu — a legendary mangal (grill) restaurant where you sit around an open fire and watch your kebabs grilled to perfection. Try the lamb ribs and beyti. Budget ~350–500 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ferries to Büyükada run several times daily — check the İDO or Şehir Hatları schedule and consider buying a return ticket in advance during peak season. The horse-drawn carriage tour of the island costs approximately 500–800 TL. Bicycle rental is around 150–200 TL for a few hours. The island gets very crowded on weekends — a Tuesday visit is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Pera Museum (Pera Müzesi) in Beyoğlu — a world-class private museum housing Orientalist paintings, Anatolian weights and measures, and Kütahya tiles. The star exhibit is Osman Hamdi Bey's iconic 'The Tortoise Trainer.' Then explore the historic Pera/Beyoğlu neighborhood's 19th-century European-style architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (İstanbul Modern) on the Bosphorus waterfront in Karaköy — Turkey's premier contemporary art museum with rotating international exhibitions and a permanent collection of Turkish modern art. The waterfront location offers stunning views.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening shopping and souvenir hunting — revisit the Grand Bazaar (open until 19:00) or browse the Arasta Bazaar behind the Blue Mosque for quality Turkish ceramics, textiles, and hand-painted tiles. Enjoy a farewell sunset from a rooftop terrace.

meals.breakfast: Van Kahvaltı Evi in Cihangir — famous for its elaborate Kurdish-style breakfast spread from Van province, with over 20 items including honey, butter, cheeses, and herbs. Budget ~250–350 TL.
meals.lunch: Lokanta Maya in Karaköy — a celebrated farm-to-table restaurant with a daily changing menu of seasonal Turkish cuisine. Excellent value for the quality. Budget ~350–500 TL per person.
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at Mikla Restaurant atop the Marmara Pera Hotel — chef Mehmet Gürs's acclaimed New Anatolian cuisine with breathtaking 360° Istanbul views. A splurge-worthy final dinner. Budget ~800–1,200 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: Van Kahvaltı Evi is very popular — arrive when it opens or expect a wait. Mikla is one of Istanbul's top restaurants — reservations are essential, book weeks in advance. If Mikla is out of budget, Nicole Restaurant or Neolokal offer similar quality at slightly lower price points. Use the afternoon shopping time to buy vacuum-packed Turkish coffee, spices, and Turkish delight to take home.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul — revisit a favorite spot or tick off anything missed. Consider a peaceful early morning visit to the Süleymaniye Mosque garden for sunrise views over the Golden Horn and city rooftops. Or simply enjoy a leisurely final Turkish breakfast at a neighborhood tea garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel (standard checkout 12:00). Store luggage with the hotel if your flight is later. Final walk through Sultanahmet, last photographs of the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia. Head to the airport via Havaist bus or metro+tram with plenty of time to spare.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry wonderful memories of 13 days in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Final full Turkish breakfast — either at the hotel or at a beloved neighborhood spot. Savor the çay, olives, white cheese, and fresh bread one last time. Budget ~150–250 TL.
meals.lunch: Quick, satisfying farewell meal — döner kebab wrap from a quality döner shop near the hotel, or a bowl of Turkish soup (işkembe or mercimek). Budget ~150–200 TL.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–3.5 hours before your flight for Istanbul Airport — it is very large and security/passport control can take significant time. The Havaist airport bus from Sultanahmet/Taksim takes approximately 45–75 minutes depending on traffic. Keep some Turkish Lira for last-minute airport purchases. Ensure you have purchased any duty-free items (Turkish tea, baklava, ceramics) before reaching the gate.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Sultanahmet district, Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Istanbul Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Istanbul Airport to your boutique hotel in Sultanahmet. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around Sultanahmet Square. Admire the exterior of the Blue Mosque and the Hagia Sophia from the plaza, soaking in your first impressions of the Historic Peninsula. Visit the nearby Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) for a short but stunning underground experience — book a priority-access ticket in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Hippodrome (Sultanahmet Meydanı), viewing the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column at dusk. Enjoy a welcome dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the Sea of Marmara.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light mezze and Turkish tea at Matbah Restaurant (inside the Ottoman Imperial Cuisine tradition, near Hagia Sophia) — arrive around 14:30 after hotel check-in
meals.dinner: Seasons Restaurant at Four Seasons Sultanahmet or Tugra Restaurant at Çırağan Palace — request a window table for Bosphorus or garden views; expect Ottoman-inspired tasting menus

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar). Confirm Basilica Cistern tickets online before arrival. Keep the first afternoon light — jet lag management is key for a 13-day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya-i Kebir Camii). Arrive at opening (08:30) with a licensed private art historian guide to beat the crowds. Explore the Byzantine mosaics, imperial galleries, and the breathtaking dome in depth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Topkapi Palace with your private guide. Explore the Imperial Treasury (home of the Spoonmaker's Diamond and Topkapi Dagger), the Harem quarters (separate ticket required), and the sacred relics pavilion. Stroll through the tulip gardens with panoramic Bosphorus views.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Grand Bazaar area for a pre-dinner atmosphere walk (closes around 19:00 on Sundays — check seasonal hours). Evening at leisure in Sultanahmet.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast at your boutique stay — Turkish-style spread with simit, white cheese, olives, honey, clotted cream, and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Konyalı Restaurant inside Topkapi Palace grounds — an Istanbul institution since 1897, offering classic Turkish cuisine with garden terrace seating
meals.dinner: Balıkçı Sabahattin — a legendary Sultanahmet fish restaurant beloved by locals and visiting dignitaries; try the sea bass in salt crust and grilled octopus

day_by_day.notes: Book Topkapi Harem tickets separately and in advance — they sell out quickly. Hire a licensed private guide for both Hagia Sophia and Topkapi for the deepest historical context. Dress modestly for Hagia Sophia (shoulders and knees covered).

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to the Istanbul Archaeological Museums (Arkeoloji Müzeleri) — a world-class complex housing the Alexander Sarcophagus, the Treaty of Kadesh, and thousands of Anatolian, Greek, and Roman artifacts. Often overlooked by tourists, this is a hidden gem of the Historic Peninsula.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü with a private culinary guide. Sample Turkish delight, saffron, dried fruits, specialty teas, and artisan spices. Cross the Galata Bridge on foot for views of the Golden Horn and watch local fishermen.
day_by_day.evening: Take a private sunset Bosphorus cruise aboard a chartered wooden gulet or luxury yacht. Sail past Dolmabahçe Palace, the Bosphorus Bridge, and yalı (waterfront mansions) as the city lights come alive.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Pandeli Restaurant above the Spice Bazaar entrance — one of Istanbul's oldest restaurants (est. 1901), famous for its turquoise-tiled dining room and classic Ottoman dishes like hünkar beğendi (sultan's delight)
meals.dinner: Dinner served aboard your private Bosphorus yacht — arrange a catered mezze and seafood spread through your hotel concierge, or dock at Bebek and dine at Bebek Balıkçısı

day_by_day.notes: The Archaeological Museums require at least 3 hours — arrive early. The Spice Bazaar is most atmospheric on weekday mornings. Book the private Bosphorus yacht at least 1 week in advance through a luxury charter company (e.g., Bosphorus Yacht Club).

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Süleymaniye Mosque — the masterpiece of Ottoman architect Mimar Sinan, perched on the Third Hill of Istanbul. Explore the mosque interior, the tombs of Suleiman the Magnificent and Hürrem Sultan, and the peaceful courtyard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walking tour of the Süleymaniye neighborhood with a local historian guide. Explore the historic hans (caravanserais), medrese courtyards, and the old book market (Sahaflar Çarşısı). Visit the Rüstem Pasha Mosque — famous for its extraordinary Iznik tile interior.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Karaköy and Galata neighborhood across the Golden Horn. Visit the Galata Tower for panoramic city views at sunset, then wander the boutique-lined streets of Karaköy.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Darüzziyafe — a restored Ottoman soup kitchen (imaret) adjacent to Süleymaniye Mosque, serving traditional Ottoman recipes in a stunning historic setting
meals.dinner: Karaköy Lokantası — a sophisticated modern Turkish bistro in Karaköy celebrated for its daily changing menu of refined Anatolian dishes; reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: The Rüstem Pasha Mosque is small but its Iznik tiles are among the finest in the world — not to be missed. Galata Tower tickets can be purchased online. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Süleymaniye hill climb.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Princes' Islands (Adalar). Take a private ferry from Kabataş pier to Büyükada (the largest island). Arrive by 09:30 for a peaceful morning before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Büyükada by horse-drawn carriage (phaeton) — the island is car-free. Visit the Aya Yorgi (St. George) Monastery on the hilltop for panoramic Marmara Sea views. Browse the island's Victorian-era mansions and waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Istanbul by 18:00. Rest and refresh at the hotel before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast (early, before ferry departure)
meals.lunch: Milto Restaurant on Büyükada waterfront — the island's finest seafood restaurant; order the grilled sea bream, shrimp güveç, and chilled rakı
meals.dinner: Matbah Restaurant, Sultanahmet — Ottoman palace cuisine in an intimate setting; try the lamb tandir and the Ottoman rice pudding dessert

day_by_day.notes: Depart Kabataş pier by 08:30–09:00 for the 1.5-hour ferry journey. Pre-book a private speedboat transfer for a more luxurious and faster crossing. The islands are extremely popular in May — book the restaurant for lunch in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to the Chora Church (Kariye Camii) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — home to the finest surviving Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, rivaling Ravenna. Engage a specialist Byzantine art guide for maximum appreciation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Fener and Balat neighborhoods — the historic Greek and Jewish quarters of Istanbul. Walk the colorful streets, visit the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople, and browse antique shops and vintage boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet for a traditional Turkish hammam experience at the Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built 1584 by Mimar Sinan) or the Ayasofya Hürrem Sultan Hamamı — the most luxurious historic bathhouse in Istanbul.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Fener & Balat neighborhood café lunch — try Balat's trendy Forno Balat for artisan sourdough and mezze, or Ayvansaray Cafe for a local börek and tea experience
meals.dinner: Asitane Restaurant near Chora Church — the world's only restaurant dedicated entirely to recreating Ottoman palace recipes from 15th–17th century imperial kitchens; extraordinary and unique

day_by_day.notes: Chora Church may have limited access depending on restoration status — verify before visiting. Book the Ayasofya Hürrem Sultan Hamamı's private VIP suite experience well in advance (it sells out weeks ahead). The Fener-Balat walk is best done in the afternoon when light is golden.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Dolmabahçe Palace in Beşiktaş — the 19th-century Ottoman imperial palace on the European Bosphorus shore. Marvel at the 4.5-ton Bohemian crystal chandelier, the ceremonial halls, and Atatürk's private quarters. Book the combined Selamlık and Harem tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Nişantaşı neighborhood — Istanbul's answer to the Left Bank. Browse luxury Turkish designers (Vakko, Beymen), visit the Istanbul Museum of Modern Art (İstanbul Modern), and stroll through Teşvikiye.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks and dinner in Beşiktaş or Ortaköy. Walk along the Bosphorus promenade near Ortaköy Mosque — one of Istanbul's most photogenic spots, especially at night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Sunset Grill & Bar in Ulus — panoramic Bosphorus views from the hillside terrace; excellent for grilled meats and contemporary Turkish cuisine
meals.dinner: Feriye Lokantası in Ortaköy — a restored 19th-century palace pavilion on the Bosphorus waterfront serving refined Ottoman-Turkish cuisine; request a waterside table

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays — this itinerary places the visit on Friday, which is correct. Photography is restricted inside the palace. Arrange a private car or taxi for the Beşiktaş/Nişantaşı day as it is a short drive from Sultanahmet.

day_by_day.morning: Private Turkish cooking class with a renowned Istanbul chef. Learn to prepare classic dishes: Turkish breakfast spread, red lentil soup, stuffed vine leaves (dolma), lamb kebab, and baklava. Classes typically held in a private kitchen in Beyoğlu or Sultanahmet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) with a private shopping guide who knows the best artisan vendors. Shop for handmade Iznik ceramics, Ottoman calligraphy, silk scarves, hand-knotted carpets, and gold jewelry. Avoid tourist traps with expert guidance.
day_by_day.evening: Explore İstiklal Avenue and the Beyoğlu district. Ride the historic Tünel funicular and the nostalgic red tram. Discover the vibrant Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage) and the Balık Pazarı (Fish Market) in Galatasaray.

meals.breakfast: Part of the cooking class experience — prepare and eat a full traditional Turkish breakfast
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you prepared in the cooking class
meals.dinner: Mikla Restaurant atop the Marmara Pera Hotel in Beyoğlu — Chef Mehmet Gürs's celebrated modern Nordic-Anatolian tasting menu with breathtaking panoramic Istanbul views; one of Turkey's finest restaurants

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least 2 weeks in advance — recommended providers include Cooking Alaturka or Les Arts Turcs in Sultanahmet. In the Grand Bazaar, a private guide dramatically improves the experience and helps with fair price negotiation. Mikla requires advance reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Edirne (2.5 hours by private car) — the former Ottoman capital. Visit the Selimiye Mosque, Mimar Sinan's own masterpiece and UNESCO World Heritage Site, which Sinan himself considered superior to the Süleymaniye. Explore with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Edirne: visit the Old Mosque (Eski Camii), the Beyazıt II Külliye (a remarkable early Ottoman social complex), and the covered bazaar. Sample Edirne's famous ciğer (liver) and tava ciğer at a local restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by private car, arriving around 19:00–20:00. Relaxed evening and early dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Ciğer Mustafa in Edirne — the city's most celebrated liver restaurant; a unique and authentic local experience
meals.dinner: Hamdi Restaurant, Eminönü — legendary kebab house with rooftop terrace overlooking the Golden Horn and Galata Bridge; try the Urfa kebab and lamb ribs

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private driver and licensed guide for the Edirne day trip. Depart by 07:30 to maximize time. The Selimiye Mosque is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the greatest works of Islamic architecture — this excursion is highly recommended for history enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts (Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi) on the Hippodrome — housing one of the world's finest collections of Islamic manuscripts, carpets, and calligraphy. Private guided tour recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Arasta Bazaar (quieter and more authentic than the Grand Bazaar) adjacent to the Blue Mosque. Shop for high-quality handmade ceramics, kilims, and textiles directly from artisan workshops. Visit the Mosaic Museum (Büyük Saray Mozaikleri Müzesi) nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Whirling Dervishes (Sema) ceremony — the mystical Sufi ritual of the Mevlevi Order. Authentic performances are held at the Hodjapasha Cultural Center or the Sirkeci Train Station hall. A profoundly moving spiritual experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Giritli Restaurant in Sultanahmet — a beloved Cretan-Greek-Turkish fusion restaurant serving a spectacular all-inclusive meze feast with wine; book ahead
meals.dinner: Seven Hills Restaurant — rooftop dining in Sultanahmet with unobstructed views of the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia illuminated at night; excellent for grilled meats and seafood

day_by_day.notes: The Sema ceremony at Hodjapasha is more intimate and authentic than larger tourist shows — book tickets online in advance. The ceremony lasts approximately 1 hour. Dress respectfully and observe in silence.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) — having seen it from outside on Day 1, now explore the interior with a specialist guide. Admire the 20,000+ hand-painted Iznik tiles, the six minarets, and the cascading domes. Visit during a non-prayer time for the best experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Yıldız Palace complex in Beşiktaş — the last imperial Ottoman palace, set in a vast forested park. Explore the Şale Pavilion (used to host Kaiser Wilhelm II and Charles de Gaulle), the imperial porcelain factory, and the tranquil gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the Pierre Loti Café in Eyüp — take the cable car up the hill to this legendary hilltop café overlooking the Golden Horn, named after the French novelist who frequented it. A quintessential Istanbul romantic experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Nicole Restaurant at Tomtom Suites, Beyoğlu — Chef Aylin Yazıcıoğlu's refined modern Turkish cuisine with a rooftop terrace; one of Istanbul's most celebrated fine dining experiences
meals.dinner: Ulus 29 — iconic Istanbul restaurant on the Bosphorus hillside in Ulus, offering contemporary Turkish cuisine, live music, and sweeping water views; a favorite of Istanbul's elite

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Mosque is closed to tourists during the five daily prayer times — plan your visit for mid-morning (around 09:30–11:30). Pierre Loti Café is best visited 30–45 minutes before sunset. The cable car (teleferik) runs from Eyüp.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Topkapi Palace Kitchens and the Imperial Stables — sections of Topkapi rarely explored in depth. Then visit the Gülhane Park adjacent to Topkapi, one of Istanbul's oldest public parks, for a peaceful morning walk with sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Asian side of Istanbul. Take a short ferry from Eminönü to Kadıköy — Istanbul's bohemian, foodie neighborhood. Wander the Kadıköy Market (Tarihi Kadıköy Çarşısı), browse independent bookshops, vinyl record stores, and artisan food stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Final luxury Bosphorus dinner cruise or return to the European side for a farewell dinner at one of Istanbul's most celebrated restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy — a legendary restaurant run by culinary anthropologist Chef Musa Dağdeviren, serving rare regional Anatolian dishes that cannot be found elsewhere; a must for serious food lovers
meals.dinner: Neolokal Restaurant at SALT Galata — Chef Maksut Aşkar's groundbreaking modern Anatolian cuisine in a stunning historic bank building; multiple international awards; tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Çiya Sofrası is arguably the most important restaurant in Turkey for understanding the depth of Anatolian cuisine — do not miss it. The Kadıköy ferry ride itself is a classic Istanbul experience (10 minutes, spectacular views). Book Neolokal weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul — leisurely hotel breakfast. Last walk through Sultanahmet: sit in the Hippodrome, have a final Turkish tea at a traditional çay bahçesi (tea garden), and revisit any favorite spots. Purchase last-minute gifts from the Arasta Bazaar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — optional visit to the Pera Museum in Beyoğlu (home of the famous 'Tortoise Trainer' painting by Osman Hamdi Bey and rotating world-class exhibitions), or a final hammam session. Private luxury transfer to Istanbul Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — flight home. Carry memories of 13 extraordinary days in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Grand final Turkish breakfast at the hotel — savor every bite: fresh simit, kaymak with honey, menemen (Turkish egg dish), börek, and Turkish tea
meals.lunch: Leb-i Derya Richmond in Beyoğlu — rooftop café with stunning panoramic views; light Turkish lunch of mezze and grilled fish before heading to the airport
meals.dinner: Airport lounge or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for Istanbul Airport (IST) — it is vast and security lines can be long. Arrange private luxury transfer in advance. Confirm all luggage weight limits if purchasing carpets, ceramics, or other souvenirs. A tip: the Turkish Lira fluctuates — settle any remaining bills and convert currency before departure.
